newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Friday with the absence of new issues and listings on the Shanghai's A share market reducing institutional liquidity demand, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract dropped to 10.21 percent from 12.99 percent on Thursday.
Total market turnover reduced to 7.78 million lots from 9.53 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"There have been no new issues and listings in the past few days in Shanghai," said one trader. "This has reduced institutional fund demand and pushed down the rates today."
"The sharp losses on the A share market today also made those institutions cut their fund borrowing," he added.
Traders said the A share market perfomance would be a key factor for the repo rate movements early next week.
Contracts on Shanghai's T-bill spot market ended mostly up due to rises in formerly less fancied contracts, traders said.
But the most active three-year bond that matures in September 1999 bucked the trend and fell to 102.25 yuan from 102.29 yuan, indicating market sentiment was weak, they said.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market shrank to a very thin 517,168 lots from 637,606.
"Falls in major contracts such as the most active three-year contract and the 10-year bond indicated market sentiment was weak," said one trader.
"Financial institutions usually do less business around the year-end, causing a lack of liquidity on the market," said a second trader.
Traders expect the contracts to move in a narrow range in thin trading early next week.
